summary.intent: The user reviewed pending todos, identified two groupings (#8+#9 as a batch and #2 as superseding #5), then created and fully planned GSD Phase 48 to consolidate folder-state ownership in the SDK and harden share metadata across three bundled todos.
summary.outcome: Phase 48 was created, researched, pattern-mapped, planned (6 plans across 3 waves), and independently verified with zero blockers. A 9-step autonomous pipeline was launched to execute the phase, push the branch, run web-e2e pre-merge, and open a PR.

repo: web-e2e runs exclusively on push to main via ci-e2e.yml (paths-filtered); this is the structural gap that let PR #498's regression land unverified

web-e2e.yml has a direct workflow_dispatch trigger with `ref: ${{ inputs.ref || github.sha }}`, so `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh workflow run web-e2e.yml --ref <branch>` runs the identical job against any pushed branch pre-merge without needing secrets:inherit

PR #498 introduced self-bootstrap for folderTree but regressed main: loadFolder does an unconditional folderTree.set() that clobbers fresher in-memory state with a stale IPNS snapshot — same desync class as PR #489

For shared-folder ownership (REQ-3), the right shape is a sibling sharedFolderTree keyed by shareId (not extending folderTree) because shared folders carry a distinct SharedWriteContext and can collide on ipnsName
The API server is zero-knowledge so cannot re-encrypt legacy plaintext itemName values; the chosen policy is lazy client-side backfill (client wraps and re-saves on next legitimate write)
TypeORM migration run command for this repo: `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api migration:run`; `pnpm api:generate` is required after any API entity/DTO changes

CRDT-IPNS inbox research (#2) would subsume the itemName encryption fix (#5) by making all inbox content ECIES-wrapped by design, but it is long-horizon research and cannot hold an open MEDIUM security finding hostage
The GSD planner's VALIDATION.md per-task table is intentionally left TBD at plan time and back-filled by /gsd:validate-phase — the plan-checker warning about this is expected and non-blocking
Phase 47 (PR #494) covered owned-folder consolidation; Phase 48 is the shared-folder and metadata-crypto layer that follows it

code.finding: Unconditional folderTree.set() in loadFolder — the root cause of the #498 regression. Fix: insert a sequenceNumber guard (if existing.sequenceNumber >= resolved, keep existing) before this call
ensureFolderLoaded short-circuit — must be left intact when applying the REQ-1 guard to avoid re-regressing #498
DFS child-check in ensureFolderLoaded — must be preserved alongside the REQ-1 fix
folder:updated event definition — direct analog for the new sharedFolder:updated event to be added for REQ-3
Write-back logic that becomes an event-fed projection in REQ-3; withConflictRetry is dropped because CAS moves into the SDK client
Wrap points for ECIES encryption of itemName (REQ-4); mirrors the encryptedKey flow already present
Migration to clone for REQ-4's nullable item_name_encrypted bytea column — additive only, no data UPDATE, zero-knowledge compliant
Already returns {publishedChildren, newSequenceNumber} via publishWithCas — the REQ-3 SDK client methods delegate to this existing function

workflow: When a pending todo is 'gated on X proving out in staging/prod,' always verify that X has actually cleared staging before treating the gate as satisfied — #498 was filed as proven-out but was actively regressing main

Grouping related todos into a phase works best when the relationship is made explicit: #8+#9 are 'do together on one branch,' while #2+#5 are 'supersession' (one would make the other redundant) and must be handled separately
The GSD pattern-mapper verifies all research line numbers against current source before handing off to the planner — ensures the planner's analog references don't point at stale locations
CONTEXT.md written before spawning the planner captures design decisions (tree-shape fork, legacy-data policy, invite-path scope) so the planner uses them as constraints rather than re-opening them

For AFK autonomous runs with signed commits, the pragmatic policy is: keep signing on, but fall back to unsigned if 1Password hangs to avoid wedging the pipeline, and flag the unsigned commits for re-sign before merge
Direct workflow_dispatch against a feature branch is faster than dispatching ci-e2e.yml because it skips the desktop-e2e job that ci-e2e.yml also triggers

friction: Stream idle timeout during the initial parallel reader fan-out (the agent investigation of the failing e2e run) — lost partial response and had to redirect to a phase-based approach
web-e2e only runs on push to main with no PR trigger — structural gap that allowed #498's regression to land; the dispatch workaround exists but is manual
1Password SSH signing is a potential AFK wedge point for unattended commit pipelines
